title: How do you listen really well?
examples: How can I be a good listener?
How do I stop interrupting people?

explain.say: Listening well is a skill you can learn. Look at the first step on the board. Look at the person talking. If that feels hard, you can look near their face.

explain.say: Next, keep your body still and face them. Let your mouth wait until they finish. Talking while someone else talks is called interrupting. It can make them feel unimportant. Try waiting until they stop.

faq.q: What does saying it back mean?
faq.a: It means repeating the main idea in your own words, like: So your puppy chewed your shoe? It shows you were really listening.
asks: Tell me about the Say it back

faq.a: Take a small breath when you want to talk, and wait for the person to finish. If you worry you will forget, hold your idea with your finger, or ask: Can I add something?
asks: Tell me about the Mouth waits

faq.q: What if looking at people feels hard?
faq.a: That is okay. Many people, including many autistic people, find eye contact uncomfortable. You can look near their face, nod, or turn your body towards them to show you are listening.
asks: Do I have to look in someone's eyes?

faq.a: Listening helps people feel cared about, helps you learn, and stops lots of mix-ups and arguments.
asks: Why should I listen to others?

faq.q: How can I show I am listening?
faq.a: Face the person, nod, make small sounds like mm-hmm, ask a question and say back what you heard.
asks: Tell me about the Nod along

facts: The saying that we have two ears and one mouth so we can listen twice as much as we speak is often credited to the Greek thinker Epictetus.
Eye contact customs differ: in some cultures, such as parts of Japan and Nigeria, children may look down when an elder speaks as a sign of respect.

quiz.say: You tell a friend some news. Which friend is listening well to you?

options.show: Looks at a game while you talk
options.say: Looks at a game while you talk

options.show: Nods and asks, what happened next?
options.say: Nods and asks, what happened next?

quiz.why: Nodding and asking a question show they care about what you say.

wrong.0: Their eyes are on the game, so their attention is somewhere else.
wrong.2: Talking over someone is interrupting. A good listener waits.

quiz.say: Your friend says, I fell off my bike and people laughed. Which answer says it back?
quiz.show: 🚲 Friend: I fell off my bike. Which says it back?

options.show: So you fell and people laughed? That sounds hard.
options.say: So you fell and people laughed? That sounds hard.

quiz.why: Saying back the main idea and naming the feeling shows you understood.

wrong.1: This changes the subject to you. Your friend wants to be heard.
wrong.2: This can sound like you do not care. Say back what you heard.
